pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

2. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

3. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

4. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

5. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.

6. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. goes

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

9. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. blue

11. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.

12. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

7. C — went

8. A — Where is the library?

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

10. C — run

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pre-Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Handwriting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
